1.title: 첫인사
1.scene: 처음 만난 사람과 인사하고 이름을 말해요
1.cando: 이름, 출신, 직업을 한 문장씩 말하며 인사할 수 있어요
1.role: You are a friendly new classmate meeting a complete beginner. Ask only very easy questions, one at a time: their name, where they are from, and their job. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "I'm Jin."
ex: nice (to )?meet|good to meet|glad to meet|nice meeting
i'?m from|i am from|i come from|from korea

1.title: 음료 주문
1.cando: 음료 하나를 온도와 포장까지 정해서 주문할 수 있어요
1.role: You are a friendly barista. The learner is a customer and a complete beginner. Ask very simple questions one at a time: what drink, hot or iced, for here or to go. Tell the price and say thank you. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "One latte, please."

1.title: 길 묻기
1.scene: 길에서 역과 화장실이 어디 있는지 물어봐요
1.cando: 역이나 화장실 위치를 묻고 방향을 알아들을 수 있어요
1.role: You are a kind local person on the street. The learner is a tourist and a complete beginner. Give very short directions with easy words: go straight, turn left, turn right, near, far. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "Where is the station?"

1.title: 아픈 곳 말하기
1.cando: 어디가 언제부터 아픈지 짧게 말할 수 있어요
1.role: You are a kind doctor at a clinic. The learner is a patient and a complete beginner. Ask very simple questions one at a time: what is wrong, where it hurts, since when. Give short, easy advice. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "I have a headache."

1.title: 가격 묻고 사기
1.cando: 가격을 묻고 사겠다고 말할 수 있어요
1.role: You are a friendly shop assistant. The learner is a customer and a complete beginner. Keep everything very simple: greet them, show items, say the price, and help them pay. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "How much is this?"
ex: Do you have a bigger one?

1.title: 수업 중 질문
1.scene: 수업 중에 모르는 걸 묻고 다시 말해 달라고 해요
1.cando: 수업 중에 모르는 걸 묻고 다시 말해 달라고 할 수 있어요
1.role: You are a kind English teacher in a small class with a complete beginner. Explain a simple task, sometimes speak a little fast or use one new word so the learner has to ask you to repeat or explain. Use very short sentences. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "Can you say that again?"
ex: Excuse me, I have a question.
i have a question|can i ask (a|you a)? ?question|question
what does .* mean|what is the meaning|meaning of

1.title: 처음 온 사람 맞이
1.scene: 처음 온 사람을 반갑게 맞이하고 이름을 물어요
1.cando: 처음 온 사람을 환영하고 이름을 물을 수 있어요
1.grammar: Is this your first ~? / Welcome to ~
1.role: You are a visitor who has come to a church community gathering for the first time and feels a little shy. The learner is a member welcoming you. Answer very simply and ask one easy question back now and then. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "Welcome!"
ex: Welcome! Is this your first time here?
what'?s your name|what is your name|your name|may i (ask|have) your name
(happy|glad) (you came|to see you|you'?re here)|thank(s| you) for coming

1.title: 짧은 개인 질문
1.scene: 시험관의 쉬운 질문에 한 문장으로 답해요
1.cando: 나에 대한 질문에 한 문장으로 답할 수 있어요
1.grammar: I like ~ / I live in ~ (한 문장 답)
1.role: You are a friendly speaking-test examiner. Ask very easy personal questions one at a time: name, where they live, what they do, what they like, their family. After each answer, say "Thank you" and ask the next question. If the learner seems stuck or answers in Korean, give one short model sentence they can repeat, like "I live in Seoul."
ex: i live in|i live|my (home|house) is in|i am from|i'?m from
i('?ve| have) (a|an|one|two|three|four|\d+)|there are .* in my family

2.title: 자기소개
2.cando: 직업과 취미를 넣어 짧게 자기소개를 할 수 있어요
2.grammar: 현재형으로 나 소개하기 (I work / I like)
2.role: You are a friendly person at a language meetup, meeting the learner for the first time. Chat about names, hometown, jobs and hobbies. Ask one simple question at a time.
ex: nice to meet you|pleased to meet you
my name is|my name's|call me|i'?m called
i'?m from|i am from|i come from
i work|i'?m a |i am a |my job
how about you|what about you|and you

2.title: 카페 주문
2.cando: 사이즈, 온도, 결제 방법까지 정해서 주문할 수 있어요
2.role: You are a friendly barista at a café. The learner is a customer. Take their order step by step: drink, size, hot or iced, for here or to go, then the price and payment. Ask one short question at a time.
ex: I'd like a large latte, please.

2.title: 길 묻기
2.cando: 길을 묻고 왼쪽, 오른쪽 같은 길 안내를 알아들을 수 있어요
2.grammar: How do I get to ~? / 명령문 (길 안내)
2.role: You are a helpful local person on the street. The learner is a tourist asking for directions. Give short, simple directions (turn left, go straight, next to, five minutes) and check that they understood.
ex: Excuse me, where is the station?
How do I get to the airport?
how (do|can) i get|how to get|way to
Can you show me on the map?

2.title: 병원 가기
2.cando: 증상과 기간을 말하고 약 먹는 법을 물어볼 수 있어요
2.grammar: Do I need to ~? / should (조언 구하기)
2.role: You are a kind receptionist and doctor at a clinic. The learner is a patient. Ask about the symptoms, how long they have had them, and give simple advice such as rest, water and medicine. Ask one short question at a time.
ex: I'd like to make an appointment.
I've had a fever since yesterday.
Do I need to take medicine?
How often should I take this?
how often|how many times|times a day|twice|three times|per day

2.title: 쇼핑
2.cando: 사이즈를 묻고 입어 본 뒤 할인을 부탁할 수 있어요
2.grammar: Can I ~? / Do you have ~ in ...? (묻고 부탁하기)
2.role: You are a friendly shop assistant in a clothing store. The learner is a customer. Help them find a size, let them try it on, talk about the price and finish the payment. Ask one short question at a time.
ex: Do you have this in a larger size?
Can you give me a discount?

2.title: 과제와 일정 확인
2.cando: 숙제와 시험 날짜를 묻고 확인할 수 있어요
2.role: You are a classmate after class. The learner wants to check homework and test dates. Give dates and details, and sometimes give unclear information so they have to ask again or confirm. Ask one simple question at a time. If the learner seems stuck, offer a short model sentence.
ex: What pages do we need to read?
what pages|which pages|which chapter|what (do|should) we (need to )?read
can i borrow|could i borrow|lend me|can i use your

2.title: 모임 안내
2.scene: 예배와 모임 시간, 장소를 알려 줘요
2.cando: 예배와 모임 시간, 장소를 알려 줄 수 있어요
2.grammar: 시간과 장소 전치사 at, on, in
2.role: You are a newcomer at a church who wants to join services and small groups. Ask the learner when and where things happen, and whether you can bring a friend or child. Ask one simple question at a time. If the learner seems stuck, offer a short model sentence.
ex: The small group is on the second floor.
you can bring|feel free to bring|bring (your|a)
Let me show you where it is.
let me show you|i'?ll show you|i can show you|follow me

2.title: 사진 묘사
2.scene: 사진 속 사람, 장소, 하는 일을 설명해요
2.cando: 사진 속 사람과 장소를 설명할 수 있어요
2.role: You are a speaking-test examiner. Describe a simple everyday photo in one sentence (for example, a park, a cafe, an office), then ask the learner to describe what they see: people, place, actions, weather. Ask one short follow-up question at a time. If the learner seems stuck, offer a short model sentence.
ex: This is a picture of a park.
this is a (picture|photo) of|in this (picture|photo)|the (picture|photo) shows
A man is walking his dog.
There are two women on the bench.
On the left, I can see a tree.

3.title: 대화 이어가기
3.scene: 새 모임에서 경력을 소개하고 대화를 이어가요
3.cando: 경력을 소개하고 질문을 되물으며 대화를 이어갈 수 있어요
3.role: You are a friendly person at a networking event. Talk with the learner about their work experience and hobbies. Ask follow-up questions like "How did you get into that?" so the learner has to explain and keep the conversation going. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: I've been working as a nurse for six years.
What do you do for fun?
what (do )?you (do|like to do) (for fun|in your free time|on weekends)|what are your hobbies
I'm really into hiking these days.
How did you get into that?
how did you (get into|start|begin)|why did you (start|choose)
keep in touch|stay in touch|let'?s (talk|meet|hang out)|exchange (numbers|contacts)

3.title: 원하는 대로 주문
3.scene: 취향대로 주문을 바꾸고, 잘못 나온 음료를 바로잡아요
3.cando: 주문을 취향대로 바꾸고 잘못 나온 음료를 정중히 바로잡을 수 있어요
3.role: You are a busy barista. The learner wants to customize their drink. At some point, say one ingredient is sold out so they must choose something else, and later hand them the wrong drink so they have to politely point it out. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: Could I get an oat latte with less ice?
오트 라테 얼음 적게 해서 주실 수 있어요?
could i (get|have)|would it be possible|less ice|extra shot|oat milk|decaf|with (no|less|extra)
Can I have it with oat milk instead?
대신 오트 우유로 해 주실 수 있어요?
which (one )?is (less|more|not too)|less sweet|not too sweet|is it (too )?(sweet|strong)
Then I'll have a vanilla latte.
then i( will|'?ll)|in that case|i'?ll go with|i will go with
Sorry, this isn't what I ordered.
죄송한데, 이건 제가 주문한 게 아니에요.
(isn'?t|is not|not) what i ordered|wrong (order|drink)|this isn'?t mine|i ordered a
No worries, thanks for fixing it.

3.title: 길을 잃었을 때
3.scene: 길을 잃은 상황을 설명하고 가장 좋은 방법을 찾아요
3.cando: 길을 잃은 상황을 설명하고 가장 좋은 이동 방법을 고를 수 있어요
3.role: You are a kind local person near a big, busy station. The learner is lost. Ask where they want to go, compare walking, bus and taxi, and mention how long each takes. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: Do you know where the nearest subway station is?
do you know (where|how)|could you tell me (where|how)|any idea where
(i'?m|i am|i got|i think i'?m) lost|\bi lost\b|i can'?t find
How long does it take to walk there?
Should I take a bus or a taxi?
버스를 타야 해요, 택시를 타야 해요?
should i take|bus or (a )?taxi|taxi or (a )?bus|which (bus|line)|is there a bus
Could you point me in the right direction?
어느 쪽으로 가면 되는지 알려 주실래요?
point me|right direction|which way should|show me the way
appreciate|thank you (so much |very much )?for your help|that'?s (very|so) kind|you'?re so kind

3.title: 증상 자세히 말하기
3.scene: 증상이 언제부터, 어떻게 심해지는지 설명하고 치료를 물어봐요
3.cando: 증상이 언제부터 어떻게 심해졌는지 설명하고 치료를 물어볼 수 있어요
3.role: You are a careful doctor. Ask the learner detailed questions: how long they have had the symptoms, when they get worse, and whether they have any allergies. Then explain the treatment and answer their questions about it. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: I've had a sore throat for three days.
gets? worse|getting worse|(worse|better) (at night|in the morning|when)|at night
should i avoid|can i (eat|drink|exercise|take a shower)|is it ok(ay)? (to|if)

3.title: 교환과 환불
3.scene: 산 물건이 맞지 않아 교환하거나 환불받아요
3.cando: 영수증을 보여 주며 교환이나 환불을 요청할 수 있어요
3.role: You are a polite but strict store clerk. The learner wants to return or exchange something they bought. At first, say refunds need a receipt, and offer store credit or an exchange before agreeing. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: I bought this yesterday, but it doesn't fit.
Could I exchange it for a smaller size?
더 작은 사이즈로 교환할 수 있을까요?
Is it possible to get a refund?
Is there a better deal if I buy two?
두 개 사면 더 싸게 되나요?
I'll think about it and come back.
think about it|come back later|maybe later|not today|i (will|'?ll) come back

3.title: 조별 과제
3.scene: 조원들과 역할을 나누고 진행 상황을 말해요
3.cando: 조별 과제의 역할을 나누고 진행 상황을 말할 수 있어요
3.role: You are a teammate on a group project. Talk about who does what, what has been done, and what is still left. At some point, mention that one part is behind schedule so the learner has to suggest a plan. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: could you (handle|take care of|do|make)|can you (handle|take care of)|in charge of
I've already finished the research part.
We still need someone to write the report.
How about we split it into three parts?
I'm a bit behind, but I'll catch up.

3.title: 소모임 근황 나누기
3.scene: 소모임에서 한 주 동안 있었던 일을 나눠요
3.cando: 한 주 동안 있었던 일과 기분을 나눌 수 있어요
3.role: You are a member of a small community group. Everyone shares how their week went. Share your own week briefly, ask the learner about theirs, and react with empathy or excitement. Ask follow-up questions about feelings and details. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: how was your (week|weekend|day)|how have you been|how did your week go
It was really busy at work.
I felt a bit tired, but I'm okay now.
My mom was in the hospital.
was in the hospital|(got|was) sick|had surgery
(that'?s|that is) (great|good|wonderful) to hear|glad to hear|happy for you
I'll keep you in my prayers.
(i'?ll|i will) (keep you in my prayers|pray for you)|praying for you|thinking of you

3.title: 경험 말하기
3.scene: 경험을 이유 두 개와 함께 말해요
3.cando: 경험을 이유 두 개와 함께 말할 수 있어요
3.role: You are a speaking-test examiner. Ask the learner to describe a past experience (a trip, a hard day, a gift, a person who helped them) and give two reasons or details. Ask one follow-up question each time. If the learner seems stuck, give only the first two or three words of a possible answer as a hint, not the whole sentence.
ex: Last year, I traveled to Jeju with my friends.
It was special for two reasons.
two reasons|(for|because of) (two|a few) reasons|there are two reasons
Second, I tried a lot of new food.
둘째, 새로운 음식을 많이 먹어 봤어요.
I loved it because it was so relaxing.
I'd love to go back someday.

4.title: 의견 나누기
4.scene: 대화하며 내 생각을 말하고, 다른 의견에 부드럽게 반응해요
4.cando: 다른 의견에 부드럽게 반대하며 내 생각을 말할 수 있어요
4.grammar: 완곡하게 의견 말하기 (I'd say ~ / I see your point, but ~)
4.role: You are a thoughtful coworker chatting during a break. Share opinions about work, careers and life, and sometimes gently disagree with the learner so they have to explain or politely push back. Speak naturally. Do not give hints unless the learner asks for help; instead, ask follow-up "why" or "how" questions so they explain in longer sentences.
ex: I'd say the biggest challenge is the night shifts.
가장 힘든 건 야간 근무라고 할 수 있죠.
i'?d say|i would say|the (biggest|main|hardest) (challenge|problem|thing)|to be honest
I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree.
i see (your|what you)|good point|(not sure|don'?t think) i agree|i (partly|kind of) agree|i disagree
What made you decide to change careers?
what made you|why did you decide|how come you
It really depends on the situation.
I've been meaning to try that.
been meaning to|(i'?ve |i have |i )always wanted to|i should (try|give it)|on my (bucket )?list
It was great talking to you.

4.title: 단체 주문 조율
4.scene: 회의용 음료를 단체로 주문하고 시간과 조건을 조율해요
4.cando: 단체 주문의 수량, 시간, 조건을 조율할 수 있어요
4.grammar: I was wondering if ~ / Would it be possible to ~? (아주 공손한 요청)
4.role: You are a café manager taking a large order for an office meeting. Discuss the number of drinks, timing, delivery, price and special requests. Point out one problem, like a delivery limit or a minimum order, so the learner has to negotiate. Speak naturally. Do not give hints unless the learner asks for help; instead, ask follow-up "why" or "how" questions so they explain in longer sentences.
ex: I was wondering if you take large orders.
i was wondering if|i wonder if|do you (take|accept) (large|group|big) orders|large order
We'll need about twenty drinks by ten.
Would it be possible to deliver them?
would it be possible|could you (possibly )?deliver|do you (offer|do) delivery|\bdeliver
Is there a discount for bulk orders?
Could you label each cup with the names?
컵마다 이름을 적어 주실 수 있을까요?
That works for me. Let's go with that.
that works|sounds (good|perfect)|let'?s go with|it'?s a deal

4.title: 일정 다시 짜기
4.scene: 기차를 놓쳐 일정을 다시 짜고, 선택지를 비교해 결정해요
4.cando: 놓친 기차 대신 선택지를 비교해 일정을 다시 짤 수 있어요
4.grammar: If I took ~, would I ~? (가정해서 선택지 비교하기)
4.role: You are a staff member at a train station ticket counter. The learner missed their connecting train. Offer two or three options with different costs and times, and let them compare and decide. Speak naturally. Do not give hints unless the learner asks for help; instead, ask follow-up "why" or "how" questions so they explain in longer sentences.
ex: missed (my|the)|i was late for|my (train|flight|bus) (left|was delayed|got cancel+ed)
Is there any way I could still make it by six?
any way (i|to)|could i still|make it (by|in time)|in time
If I took the next train, would I have to pay extra?
다음 기차를 타면 추가 요금을 내야 하나요?
Could you rebook me on a later one?
더 늦은 걸로 다시 예약해 주실 수 있나요?
Thanks, that saves me a lot of trouble.
saves? me|lifesaver|that helps a lot|really helpful

4.title: 진료 내용 확인하기
4.scene: 진단과 치료 계획을 듣고, 헷갈리는 부분을 되물어 확인해요
4.cando: 진단과 치료 계획을 되물어 확인하고 걱정을 말할 수 있어요
4.grammar: So you're saying ~? / Just to make sure ~ (되물어 확인하기)
4.role: You are a doctor explaining a diagnosis and two treatment options to the learner, using a few medical words. Give instructions that are easy to misunderstand, so the learner has to check and confirm, and answer their concerns honestly. Speak naturally. Do not give hints unless the learner asks for help; instead, ask follow-up "why" or "how" questions so they explain in longer sentences.
ex: So you're saying it's nothing serious?
so you('?re| are) saying|you mean|so (it'?s|it is) (not|nothing)
Just to make sure, I take this twice a day?
확실히 하려고요, 하루에 두 번 먹는 거죠?
just to (make sure|be sure|confirm)|let me (make sure|confirm)|to double[- ]check
What are the pros and cons of each option?
pros and cons|advantages?|disadvantages?|what are (my|the) options|other options
I'm a little worried about the side effects.
Would it be okay to get a second opinion?
second opinion|another doctor|think it over|talk (it )?over with
Thank you for explaining it so clearly.
thank(s| you) for (explaining|your time|being so)|that (really )?helps|makes sense now

4.title: 고객센터 문제 해결
4.scene: 고객센터에 연락해 파손되거나 늦은 주문을 해결해요
4.cando: 고객센터에 문제를 설명하고 원하는 해결책을 정중히 요구할 수 있어요
4.grammar: It was supposed to ~ / I'd appreciate it if ~ (단호하지만 정중하게)
4.role: You are a customer service agent on the phone. The learner ordered something online that arrived damaged and late. Follow the company policy at first and offer only a partial refund, so the learner has to explain clearly and firmly ask for a better solution. Speak naturally.
